sc: 9-month-old, increasing pallor, huge spleen, frontal bossing, target cells, HbF 90% → β-thalassaemia major
Boy, 2 days after eating fava beans, sudden pallor, cola-coloured urine, bite cells → G6PD deficiency
Father had splenectomy, child with jaundice, splenomegaly, spherocytes, Coombs negative → Hereditary spherocytosis
f: Pallor, jaundice, splenomegaly, gallstones · high retics, high unconjugated bilirubin, high LDH · crises: aplastic, haemolytic, sequestration
CBC, retics, film, bilirubin · direct Coombs (immune) · Hb electrophoresis · G6PD assay · EMA test (spherocytosis)
Presents 6–12 months · hair-on-end skull · HbF high · transfuse to pre-Hb 9.5–10.5 · chelate when ferritin > 1000 (deferasirox)
Microcytosis, high RBC count, normal ferritin · HbA2 > 3.5% · no iron
G6PD: avoid fava beans, primaquine, sulfonamides · AIHA: Coombs +, spherocytes → prednisolone · cold: mycoplasma
Iron overload (heart, liver, puberty) · hypersplenism · gallstones · infections after splenectomy
trap: Never give iron in thalassaemia major (ferritin high) · spherocytes in HS and AIHA: the Coombs test separates them · no splenectomy before 5–6 years
